cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

How is the value of a subscriber's monthly box measured?
cards.back:
Contribution margin: price minus cost per box: $30 − $18 = $12 (40%).

Revenue is not the basis, because the $18 cost is paid on every box.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

How is lifetime value computed on margin, and what moves it?
cards.back:
LTV = margin per month × expected lifetime: $12 × 12.5 ≈ $150.

Lifetime ≈ 1/churn, so lower churn raises LTV: 6% churn gives about $200.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

What lifetime does a monthly churn rate imply, and the reverse?
cards.back:
Lifetime ≈ 1 / monthly churn: 8% gives about 12.5 months.

Reverse: a 12.5-month lifetime implies churn of about 8% per month.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

How many months does a new subscriber take to repay acquisition cost, and what cash does that imply?
cards.back:
Payback = CAC / monthly margin: $60 / $12 = 5 months.

→ Each new subscriber is a cash outflow for those 5 months.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

Is LTV/CAC of 2.5 enough to scale paid acquisition, and what does payback add?
cards.back:
Rule of thumb: at least 3 before scaling; $150 / $60 = 2.5 is below it.

Payback of 5 months adds the cash view: fast growth burns cash even when LTV/CAC looks fine.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

What does one average churn rate hide, and how do cohort curves show it?
cards.back:
First-month churn is usually far above later churn, so an average hides it.

Cohort retention curves, one per signup month, show where the drop-off happens.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

What does LTV computed on revenue instead of margin do to the estimate?
cards.back:
Overstatement: revenue is $30 and margin $12, so LTV on revenue is 2.5× too high.

→ Value must use margin, the money left after the cost per box.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

What can a blended CAC hide, and how should acquisition cost be measured instead?
cards.back:
Blended CAC averages all channels, so a cheap channel can mask an expensive one.

→ Measure CAC by channel and by cohort, using same-period spend and new subscribers for each.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

Northwind wants to double ad spend. What should decide it, given CAC and LTV/CAC?
cards.back:
Two problems: CAC usually rises with spend, since the cheapest audiences are reached first.

→ At 8% churn, LTV/CAC is about 2.5, below the rule-of-thumb 3.

cards.front:
[Macro] Business&Management: unit economics

Is the annual plan's discount worth the lower margin, given that it also brings the cash forward?
cards.back:
Open question: not yet resolved.

Weigh the discount against the lower margin per box and the cash received upfront.
